name: Venice, Italy

sights.name: Lace Museum
sights.hours: Apr-Oct: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00; Nov-Mar: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00; ticket office closes 30 min earlier; closed Mon, Dec 25, Jan 1, May 1 closed
sights.content: There is a small lace museum called Museo del Merletto. Opinions on it vary from "not much to see" to "I didn't think I was interested in lace, but I spent 90 minutes in there".  A MUVE museum.

foodDrink.name: Trattoria da Romano
foodDrink.content: Famous people, including royalty, visited the place. The walls are covered with their photo's.

sights.name: Piazza Ferretto
sights.content: A typically Italian piazza, with a modern water feature at the center and lots of different eateries with outside seating. It is also full of top end designer stores.

sights.name: Parco San Giuliano
sights.content: A local park worth visiting. It is often used for outdoor concerts in the summer. It also has a remarkable and unique view of Venice lagoon as it borders the Ponte della Liberta, which joins the Venetian islands with the mainland.

sights.name: Parco Bissuola
sights.content: Another local park worth visiting. It offers good sport facilities and an outdoor pool.

foodDrink.name: Brothers Fast Food & Namaste Indian Restaurant
Pasticceria Serenissima
foodDrink.content: A 30-year-old patisserie. Specialities: Hazelnut cakes, ice creams and Easter eggs.

sights.name: Archaeological Museum
sights.content: Collection of Greek and Roman finds, archaeological finds from the estuary from Paleo-Veneto and Etruscan periods.

sights.name: Chiesa di Santa Fosca
sights.content: Has the form of a Greek cross, which is surrounded by a semi-octagonal porticus.

foodDrink.name: Ristorante al Trono di Attila
foodDrink.hours: Lunch daily; May-Sep:  evenings Fri Sat  and by reservation (min. 8/10 people)

sights.name: Saint Anthony's cathedral
sights.content: Saint Anthony's Basilica is the best-known tourist site in Padova - millions of pilgrims visit every year. Built immediately after "The Saint's" death in the 1200s, it houses his tomb and notable relics. The statues and crucifix on the main

sights.name: Scrovegni Chapel
sights.price: €14 full price, €5 student price (''including Eremitani Civic Museum and Contemporary Art Museum'')
sights.content: The Chapel is in the north of the city center, not far from the bus and train stations. The walls and ceilings are covered in frescos by Giotto, completed in 1303-1305. The chapel has been well preserved and the art is very impressive. Some

sights.name: Astronomic Observatory
sights.content: Although the observatory was built after Galileo's time in Padua, you'll learn a lot about his significance for the research in Padua. You reach the top of the tower after a lecture of about one hour and can enjoy the view. ''Tickets at the

sights.name: Palazzo della Ragione
sights.content: The large building located between Piazza della Frutta and Piazza delle Erbe. Its ground floor hosts small market shops. The upper floor is a single large hall housing artwork and occasional exhibitions.

sights.name: Botanic Garden
sights.content: The world's oldest still operating botanic garden, operated by the University of Padua, and on the UNESCO World Heritage list since 1997. It is not large, but is subtly laid out to swallow groups of people and give the impression of solitud

sights.name: Eremitani Civic Museum
sights.content: The museum is divided into an archeological section and a picture gallery, which has a very important collection with Tizian, Tintoretto, Giotto and Bellini among other important painters.

piers.name: Isola di San Francesco del deserto

guideSights.name: Galleria Giorgio Franchetti Ca' d'Oro
guideSights.note: A collection of paintings and statues in a former palace from the 15th century. One of the best examples of Gothic architecture in Venice, sculptures, bronzes, paintings of Mantegna, Giorgione and Titian, Flemish and Dutch paintings.

guideSights.name: Oratorio dei Crociferi
guideSights.note: Small oratory facing the old monastery dei Crociferi, painting circle by Palma the Younger.

guideSights.name: Santa Maria dei Miracoli
guideSights.note: A perfect jewel box church, simple in form but ornamented with fine exterior marble facings.

guideSights.name: San Giovanni e Paolo
guideSights.note: A fine, huge Dominican church with the tombs of many Doges. It shares its piazza with the fine Renaissance façade of the Scuola San Marco and an equestrian statue of the mercenary captain Bartolomeo Colleoni (see below).

guideSights.name: Santa Maria della Pietà
guideSights.note: A church that used to house an orphanage and hospital in the 18th century, it is known among classical music enthusiasts as the church where the Catholic priest and composer Antonio Vivaldi worked for most of his career.

guideSights.name: S. Maria Formosa
guideSights.note: The first church dedicated to "Mary of the Forms" was built on this spot in the VII century, when the Virgin ordered bishop Magnus to erect one, appearing to him as an exceedingly shapely woman. The current building, planned by Codussi, dat

guideSights.name: Basilica di San Pietro di Castello
guideSights.note: Venice cathedral up to 1807, when the see was transferred to San Marco.

guideSights.name: Museo Diocesano
guideSights.note: Religious furniture and objects from now demolished churches and convents, one of the most appealing Romanesque cloisters of Venice.

guideSights.name: Museo Storico Navale
guideSights.note: Collection of relics from the Serenissima Republic of Venice, the Italian navy, and the ancient Arsenale shipyards, miniature models, uniforms and stadarts, collection of sea shells. ''The main building of the Naval Historical Museum (Riva

guideSights.name: Fondazione Querini Stampalia
guideSights.note: Residence-museum of the Querini-Stampa family, library, picture gallery, furniture and household objects from the 16th cent onwards, important paintings by Bellini, Palma, Ricci, Tiepolo and Longhi.

guideSights.name: Byzantine Pictures Museum (Greek Institute)
guideSights.note: Collection of Greek, Cretan and Venetian icons of the 14th to 18th century.

guideSights.name: Palazzo Grimani
guideSights.note: A jewel of Renaissance architecture that was opened as a Venetia civic museum in 2008, collections of paintings, archaeological collection of Greek and Roman artefacts, temporary exhibitions.

guideSights.name: Scuola Dalmatina di San Giorgio e Trifone
guideSights.note: Famous painting cycle by Vittore Carpaccio depicting the lives of St.George, Tryphon and Jerome.

guideSights.name: ASAC Library
guideSights.note: An annex at the Biennale gardens where the Biennale keeps records related to the Biennale exhibitions and to 20th century art, from 1895 onwards.

guideSights.name: Monument for Giovanni Caboto
guideSights.note: Venetian explorer of North America who worked for the British (c. 1450-c. 1500).

guideSights.name: I Gesuati
guideSights.note: 18th-century Dominican church on the Giudecca canal. The classical style building has a well-lit interior and is exceptional in preserving its original layout and Rococo decoration intact. The church and almost all its sculpture and paintin

guideSights.name: S. Maria della Salute
guideSights.note: As a votive offering for the city's deliverance from the Black Plague, the church was designed in the then fashionable Baroque style. Construction began in 1631. Most of the objects of art housed in the church bear references to the Black D

guideSights.name: Santa Maria del Carmelo church
guideSights.note: Large 14th-century Roman Catholic church.

guideSights.name: Punta della Dogana
guideSights.note: Former customs house, centre for contemporary art, permanent exhibition of works from the François Pinault Collection. Renovation by world renowned architect Tadao Ando.

guideSights.name: Ca' Rezzonico - Museum of 18th Century Venice
guideSights.note: Museum of the 18th century in Venice - attempts to revive the domestic atmosphere of Venetian nobilities. Furniture, interior decoration, paintings by Guardi, Canaletto, Tiepolo. On the third floor important paintings of the Venetian school

guideSights.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
guideSights.note: Venice's most significant art museum which is also one of Italy's best. Among the most important paintings in the Accademia are: Gentile Bellini: ''Procession on St. Mark’s Square'' (1496) and ''Miracle of the Cross at the Bridge of S. Lore

guideSights.name: Gallery Palazzo Cini
guideSights.note: Former residence of Italian industrialist ''Vittorio Cini'' who amassed large collection of Italian art. The gallery houses a collection of 15th and 16th cent paintings from Tuscany and Ferrara, period furniture, silver, ivory and ceramic o

guideSights.name: The Peggy Guggenheim Museum
guideSights.note: Offers a personal collection of modern art collected by Peggy Guggenheim. Peggy was an American married to modern artist Max Ernst, and funded a number of his contemporaries. The gallery includes a sculpture garden and works by Picasso, Kan

guideSights.name: Scuola Grande dei Carmini
guideSights.note: Painting cycles dedicated to the Madonna del Carmine, canvases by Tiepolo and Padoviano.

guideSights.name: Le Macchine di Leonardo a Venezia
guideSights.note: An exhibition in the '''Chiesa di San Barnaba''' showing around forty models of machines reproduced from Leonardo's codices. Some of the exhibits are interactive and copies of the codices are available for further reading. The church is an

guideSights.name: Rialto Bridge
guideSights.note: The bridge has become one of Venice's most recognizable icons and has a history that spans over 800 years. Today's Rialto Bridge was completed in 1591 and was used to replace a wooden bridge that collapsed in 1524.

guideSights.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
guideSights.note: A masterpiece of Tintoretto, this guild house is an exquisite example of Mannerist art at its best. In order to allow a comfortable admiration of the detailed ceiling, mirrors are offered to the visitors. Cycles of allegories, life and pass

guideSights.name: Scuola Grande di San Giovanni Evangelista
guideSights.note: Monumental staircase by Codussi, splendid San Giovanni Salon, Oratory of the Cross with precious reliquiaries.

guideSights.name: House of Carlo Goldoni
guideSights.note: Birthplace of Venice's most famous playwright. Museum, library and theater studies center. A MUVE museum.

guideSights.name: Leonardo da Vinci Museum Venice
guideSights.note: Small museum dedicated to the life and work of Leonardo da Vinci.

guideSights.name: San Giacomo di Rialto
guideSights.note: This church is possibly the oldest church in Venice built around 421. It is most recognized for its 15th-century clock above the entrance of the church. It is also recognized for the red pillars and beautiful gold accents around the church

guideSights.name: Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari
guideSights.note: The big friary church, fine example of Venetian Gothic architecture, with fine monuments and paintings of Titian, Belliniand Donatello, among which the famous 'Assunta' by Titian.

guideSights.name: San Simeone Piccolo
guideSights.note: The last church built in Venice. One of the things that it is recognized for is the fact that they celebrate Tridentine Mass on Sundays. It is also recognized for its dome because it is used to make the church look taller than it is and the

guideSights.name: Natural History Museum
guideSights.note: 11 exhibition halls with sections on palaeontology, explorations and nature. A MUVE museum.

guideSights.name: Mocenigo Palace Museum
guideSights.note: A collection of clothes dating from the 18th century. Splendid interior. Collection of dresses and accessories, fabrics, books, figurines in various period costumes. A MUVE museum.

guideSights.name: Ca' Pesaro - International Modern Art Gallery
guideSights.note: Modern art collection, paintings of the 19th and 20th century. A MUVE museum.

guideSights.name: Ca' Pesaro - Museum of Oriental Art
guideSights.note: Beautiful palace housing the gallery of modern art focusing on Italian art in the 19th century as well as the Marco Polo Museum, a rich collection mainly of Asian exhibits (fabrics, clothes, armours, porcelain). A MUVE museum.

guideSights.name: Doge's Palace
guideSights.note: Don't miss the guided tour named ''Secret Itinerary'', which will let you discover the part of the palace where the city's administration worked, as well as Casanova's jail and the wonderful five hundred year old roof structure. A MUVE muse

guideSights.name: Bell tower of St. Mark
guideSights.note: The current tower dates from 1912; an exact replica of the previous tower which collapsed in 1902. The top of the tower offers great views of Venice and the lagoon.

guideSights.name: Clock tower
guideSights.note: Having been closed for restoration for many years, the restored astronomical clock is now visible. The fascinating tour of the clock mechanism (and rooftop bell) can only be visited on a guided tour, in English: M-W at 10:00 and 11:00, on o

guideSights.name: Ponte di Rialto
guideSights.note: The bridge has become one of Venice's most recognizable icons and has a history that spans over 800 years. Today's Rialto Bridge was completed in 1591 and was used to replace a wooden bridge that collapsed in 1524.

guideSights.name: Saint Mark's Basilica
guideSights.note: Saint Mark's Basilica is on the Piazza San Marco and is one of the highlights of a visit to Venice. As with most churches in Italy, you must be dressed appropriately to be allowed in; this means no short skirts or bare shoulders. You are no

guideSights.name: Basilica San Giorgio Maggiore
guideSights.note: Designed by Andrea Palladio and build 1566-1610. Very nice views of Venice from the bell tower.

guideSights.name: S. Salvatore
guideSights.note: Includes the tomb of Caterina Cornaro, Queen of Cyprus (1454-1510).

guideSights.name: Correr Museum
guideSights.note: Interesting collection of globes, starting from the 16th century. There is also an only library hall, an archeological museum of Roman antiques and an important picture gallery. The museum offers a tour of Venetian history. Remarkable paint

guideSights.name: Palazzo Grassi
guideSights.note: Contemporary art museum. Temporary exhibitions from François Pinault's Collection.

guideSights.name: Palazzo Fortuny
guideSights.note: Collection of paintings and lamps. A MUVE museum.

guideSights.name: Scala Contarini del Bovolo
guideSights.note: A cylindrical tower with a spiralling series of arches, among the most characteristic examples of Venetian architecture at the period of transition from Gothic to Renaissance styles. From the top there are great panoramic views of the city.

guideSights.name: Music Museum
guideSights.note: Beautiful church, collection of musical instruments, Venetian Baroque paintings. [https://www.interpretiveneziani.com/en/ Interpreti Veneziani], the creators of the Music Museum, also offer concerts in the nearby San Vidal church.

guideSights.name: Archaeological Museum
guideSights.note: Collection of ancient Greek and Roman sculptures, Egyptian, Assyrian and Babylonian artefacts.

guideSights.name: Marciana National Library
guideSights.note: Buildings by Sansovino, most important collection of books in Venice.

guideSights.name: Lace Museum
guideSights.note: There is a small lace museum called Museo del Merletto. Opinions on it vary from "not much to see" to "I didn't think I was interested in lace, but I spent 90 minutes in there".  A MUVE museum.

guideSights.name: Basilica dei Santa Maria e San Donato
guideSights.note: Known for its twelfth-century Byzantine mosaic pavement, which is a similar floor to Venice's Basilica di San Marco, and the mosaic dome in the apse of the Virgin Mary. It is said to house the bones of the dragon slain by Saint Donatus. The

guideSights.name: Chiesa di San Pietro Martire
guideSights.note: Built in the 15th century and then reconstructed some years later after a fire. Inside are some art works, such as two canvasses by Bellini.

guideSights.name: Palazzo Da Mula
guideSights.note: The summer residence of the Venetian patricians. The façade features large Gothic windows and Veneto-Byzantine patere and panels from the 12th and 13th centuries. It is one of the few palazzi which escaped the restructuring of the island in

guideSights.name: Glass Museum
guideSights.note: Housed in the large Palazzo Giustinian near the island's center. "Museo Vetrario" in Italian, offers a century-by-century tour of Venetian glass-making. Roman glass pieces dating to the 1st to 3rd cent AD. Largest collection of historical g

guideSights.name: Old Jewish Cemetery - Lido
guideSights.note: Over thousand tombstones dating from 1550 to early 18th century. Guided tours on Sat from May to Oct (Italian and English), booking required.

guideSights.name: Venice Lido Planetarium
guideSights.note: Optical-mechanical structure, realistic reproduction of the celestial globe.

guideSights.name: Mekhitarist Monastery
guideSights.note: Library with historical manuscripts, collection of works, miniatures and documents of the Armenian history, Monastery Church. Tours in Italian, English, and Armenian. On the small island of San Lazzaro degli Armeni.
